title: An oval's own border hugs the oval, not the box round it
goal: A border added to an ellipse is drawn as a second oval inset inside the first one, which only looks right on a circle. On a wide oval the line drifts by a fraction of a pixel along the flanks, so the ring is not quite parallel to the shape it is going round. Make it follow the curve the way a border on a path already does.
notes:
Reproduced on 2026-09-13 while building Turn Into Path. Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/TurnIntoPathRenderTests.swift wideOvalRing composites a 200x100 ellipse with a 4pt inside border twice, once as an ellipse and once as the path it turns into, and 3471 of 288000 bytes differ with a worst channel difference of 51 of 255. Every other shape in that suite is identical or differs by 1 or 2 on a few dozen samples.

Where it is: DocumentRenderer.ringed, the shape == .ellipse branch. The BAND is drawn by drawEllipseRing, which strokes the ellipse inscribed in bounds.insetBy(width/2) — a bounding-box inset rather than the true offset curve. The masks laid handles are worse: filledEllipse(in: outerRect) and filledEllipse(in: outerRect.insetBy(width)). All three are exact on a circle and approximate on anything else.

The machinery to fix it already exists and is tested: DocumentRenderer.pathSilhouette takes a PathContent and a signed reach and hands back the true offset silhouette, by sweeping the outline with a disc (a stroke of twice the reach IS that sweep). PathContent.ellipse(in:) in ShapeToPath.swift builds the oval as four smooth anchors. So the ellipse branch could go through the same pair the path branch does and the approximation disappears. Watch the ring cache: the path route bakes per ring rather than reusing ringCache, so check RenderPerfTests before and after.
acceptance: A border on a 2:1 oval sits the same distance from the curve all the way round, checked by sampling the rendered pixels rather than by eye
A circle is unchanged, byte for byte, because it was already right
Turning an oval into a path leaves the picture identical, which it does not quite do today

log.note: duplicate of an-oval-s-outside-border-meets-the-oval-cleanly, which is the same inset-oval geometry seen from the other side; its two extra acceptance items were merged there
